title: Choose the showcase composition
question: The border-beam demo has three comp-first directions. Choose one, combine elements, or re-roll.

options.label: Upstream Specimen
options.thesis: Let the component perform first, then let the page explain it.
options.viewport: A sparse top bar leads to a two-column hero: oversized Border beam type on the left and a large live chat specimen on the right. Rotate/Pulse tabs sit directly beneath it, followed by a measured example row, playground, and install block.
options.risk: Familiar to the reference; it wins on clarity and component fidelity.
options.case: The safest way to make the demo feel like a component site instead of a generic landing page.

options.label: GPU Workbench
options.lineage: shader inspection tools and browser devtools
options.thesis: Make the rendering mechanism part of the thing visitors are exploring.
options.viewport: A compact header opens into a persistent left preview rail and a right inspector with Rotate/Pulse tabs, layer toggles, color variant controls, and a live JSX/WGSL snippet. The first fold proves three GPU layers without burying the beam.
options.risk: Can feel like tooling rather than a polished registry showcase if the inspector gets louder than the live effect.
options.case: Best for making vgpu legible as a real implementation choice, not a hidden dependency.

options.label: Moving Ribbon
options.lineage: editorial specimen sheets and kinetic typography
options.thesis: Turn the beam's motion into the page's reading rhythm.
options.viewport: A full-width hero places Border beam on one oversized line beside a single wide live specimen. A vertical Rotate/Pulse index anchors the page edge; subsequent examples appear as editorial strips with concise code annotations and a compact playground.
options.risk: The warm editorial treatment may compete with the dark, technical feel of the upstream component.
options.case: Strongest compositional departure while preserving a component-first reading order.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean component page with a hero, example grid, playground, and install command.
canonCard.viewport: Centered title, one demo card, a conventional responsive grid, then controls and installation.
canonCard.risk: Clear but indistinguishable from other component galleries.
